values.text: We possess a discerning eye for opportunities, coupled with decisive action. From early investments to enduring partnerships, we stand by you through the exhilarating peaks and inevitable valleys.

people.name: Alfred Zaccagnino
people.bio:
Alfred Zaccagnino, the President and Founder of Samarian, has guided the company's global growth, forging new horizons through strategic partnerships at home and abroad. His unique personal touch and the company's boutique approach ensure a deep understanding of clients' unique needs.

Alfred possesses an extraordinary knack for uncovering innovative investment opportunities across diverse industries. His consultancy for the Supreme Committee for Delivery and Legacy was pivotal in bringing the 2022 FIFA World Cup™ to the Middle East, a historic first.

Alfred is a dedicated philanthropist, committed to empowering underserved communities. He proudly supports the Global Sustainability Network (GSN), a global alliance of 500+ change-makers striving to eliminate extreme poverty, reduce inequality, and combat climate change by 2030. He also champions Hank's Yanks, a youth baseball team for at-risk kids, and consistently contributes resources to the Kips Bay Boys & Girls Club, providing guidance to inner-city youth aged 6–18.

people.name: Phil Leseur
people.bio:
In 2010, Phil Leseur joined Samarian Group, bringing his wealth of legal expertise to the team. His educational journey began at Queen's University in Kingston, Ontario, where he pursued his undergraduate degree and earned a Bachelor of Arts (Honours) with a major in Political Studies. He then returned to his hometown, Victoria, British Columbia, to attend law school at the University of Victoria, where he obtained his law degree.

Phil embarked on his legal career at the prestigious Vancouver law firm of Russell & DuMoulin, now part of the Canadian national law firm Faskens. His practice primarily focused on corporate and real estate law, and he played a significant role in transformative projects like the Coal Harbour and Yaletown developments, which reshaped Vancouver's downtown core.

In 2004, Phil transitioned to in-house counsel for the Bear Mountain partnership, overseeing all legal matters related to the Bear Mountain real estate and resort development in Victoria, British Columbia. This project marked the largest of its kind in Western Canada.

In 2008, Phil took on the monumental task of acquiring the National Hockey franchise, the Tampa Bay Lightning. He represented the buying group, collaborating closely with the law firm Weil Gotshal & Manges LLP's Dallas office, who served as lead counsel for the buying group. Phil managed the legal team working with the majority partner of the buying group and liaised with legal representatives of the National Hockey League and the financing entity, Galatioto Sports Partners. His work extended into 2010 when he collaborated with the New York office of the law firm Hiscock & Barclay (now Barclay Damon LLP) and lead counsel Bob Lanza for the sale of the Tampa Bay Lightning, followed by arbitration before NHL Commissioner Gary Bettman.

In 2011, Phil returned to a full-time role at the Bear Mountain development. He initially worked with the Court Appointed Monitor and later with an HSBC subsidiary company, which assumed control and ownership of the Bear Mountain real estate development and resort project. His focus was on formulating a 'workout' plan for the redevelopment and sale of the Bear Mountain project. In 2013, he became a consultant for Ecoasis, which had real estate projects in Hawaii and Whistler, British Columbia, and acquired the Bear Mountain real estate and resort development from the HSBC subsidiary.

As the Legal Advisor for The Samarian Group of Companies, Phil plays a pivotal role in advising on corporate structure, tax efficiency, compliance, financing documentation, and contractual drafting.

people.name: Micaela Mangot
people.bio:
Micaela Mangot brings a vibrant and diverse skill set to her role as VP of Global Business Development at Samarian Group. Her dynamic portfolio includes executing Samarian's business development strategy, implementing operations strategy, and nurturing investor relationships. Currently, she is focused on serving as a resource for portfolio companies assisting with critical operations such as hiring, business development, marketing, and networking.

Before joining Samarian Group, Ms. Mangot honed her skills in Product Management within KPMG's On-Demand Technology team. Wearing multiple hats, she crafted go-to-market strategies for tech solutions and contributed to enhancing existing SaaS offerings. Her tech journey included self-learning in Natural Language Generation and SaaS system navigation.

Micaela's love for learning is at the core of her identity. She proudly holds a Bachelor of Science degree from New York University and maintains a keen interest in emerging technology startups, staying abreast of the industry's latest trends.

In her leisure time, she's an avid traveler and cultural explorer, immersing herself in diverse cuisines and traditions. As a global citizen, Micaela continually forges relationships and embarks on new ventures across the world.

people.name: Jennifer Barone
people.bio:
Jennifer Barone Percontino is the Finance and Operations Manager at the Samarian Group of Companies. In her current role, she plays a pivotal part in ensuring the company's performance and efficiency. Jennifer meticulously manages financial and business records, as well as the issuance and receipt of statements for the Samarian Team.

With over 15 years of experience spanning finance, business planning, budgeting, human resources, and administration, Jennifer brings a multifaceted skill set to her role. Her keen focus on detail and precision sets her apart. Prior to her tenure with Samarian Group, she was an entrepreneur who successfully owned and operated businesses, gaining valuable insights into the art of accurate accounting while always prioritizing the broader interests of the business. Before her entrepreneurial journey, Jennifer held diverse positions in HR, Finance, and Accounting departments at BMW North America, ET Management, Inc., and Molfetta Corp.

Educated at Ramapo College of New Jersey, Mrs. Percontino continues to uphold the qualities of integrity, credibility, and dedication that have been a hallmark of her career. Beyond her professional endeavors, she finds joy in music, sports, and cherishing quality time at the beach with her two children, husband, and extensive family.

people.name: Milène Jardine
people.bio: Milène Jardine is an award-winning leader, entrepreneur, and relationship builder who helps large and small companies develop and implement brand strategies. Milène spent 12+ years overseeing international production and building private labels for Macy's resulting in hundreds of millions of dollars in annual sales. Recently, Milène created her own business consulting firm and bespoke chocolate company.

people.name: Wolfgang Heimerl
people.bio:
Wolfgang Heimerl serves as Senior Counsel and a seasoned litigator for the Samarian Group and its affiliated entities. His unique blend of education and early career experiences perfectly align with his role at Samarian Group.

He embarked on his educational journey at the W. Paul Stillman School of Business at Seton Hall, graduating with top honors, magna cum laude, with a B.S. in Accounting. This foundation in corporate finance laid the groundwork for his subsequent career, which gracefully straddled the intricate worlds of accounting and law.

During his final two years at Seton Hall, Wolfgang Heimerl honed his legal skills by clerking for Kleinberg, Kaplan, Wolff & Cohn, P.C. (KKW&C), a reputable law firm based in midtown Manhattan. Here, he swiftly gained expertise in hedge fund formation and representation. Mr. Heimerl soon transitioned to a role in the litigation department, tackling regulatory compliance and commercial transactions. After five years at KKW&C, he emerged as a more astute and accomplished attorney.

For over a decade, Mr. Heimerl has been a steadfast representative of Samarian Group principals. His work with the company has led to a multitude of diverse client transactions and projects. To master the legal landscape both domestically and globally, Wolfgang believes in ongoing study and a holistic strategy—a key differentiator of Samarian Group. He describes the company as a “brain trust,” a collective alliance of partners with a common purpose.

people.name: Major General John F. Wharton
people.bio:
Major General John F. Wharton (U.S. Army Ret.) has dedicated over three decades to serving the Nation, retiring with extensive experience in leadership, technology, innovation, and logistics. He currently advises both public and private sector organizations on national security and technology acceleration, and is a Partner at One Defense, an initiative aimed at advancing defense technology through collaboration among DOD stakeholders, industry, startups, venture capital, and academia.

Previously, General Wharton was the Commanding General of the United States Army Research, Development and Engineering Command, leading 13,800 personnel and managing 75% of the Army's R&D budget. His achievements include winning and leading five of the seven President's National Manufacturing Innovative Institutes and developing international science and technology roadmaps. His prior roles include Commanding General of the U.S. Army Sustainment Command and Chief of Staff at the U.S. Army Materiel Command, among others. General Wharton holds degrees from the United States Military Academy and the Naval War College and has served as a Visiting Senior Research Fellow at the National Defense University.
